text:
ammar: Postmortem follow-up — yesterday's auth token TTL surge from vendor-omi caused a ~45m window of elevated 401s hitting model-registry and hosted inference routes. We need clear remediation owners, timelines, and a short plan to avoid recurrence.

oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2026-374 created: auth-provider-throttle -> cascading 401s. Summary + logs in /incidents/2026/374 (internal link).

sasha: I pulled the postmortem draft into the repo: https://redwood.internal/pm/2026-374 — TL;DR: vendor-side token issuance spike + our aggressive per-request validation = cache stampede.

lizzie: Agree with the cache-stampede hypothesis. Short-term: enable token-response caching for model-registry auth (30s) and add jitter to refreshes. Who can own the short-term patch?

raj: I can take short-term patching. Plan: implement in-service token cache with per-host LRU, add jitter to refresh ±10s, and a fallback to cached token when vendor returns 5xx/429. Will open PR tonight. ETA: PR by 2026-03-27 EOD, deploy to staging 3/28.

maria: I'll own alerting + playbook updates: add metric `auth.token.refresh_errors` and threshold >5/min triggers automated circuit break to vendor and route to local fallback token service. ETA: alert + playbook draft by 2026-03-29.

ammar: Long-term items we discussed in PM: 1) vendor contract SLA/penalties + dedicated auth endpoints, 2) fallbacks for model-registry to use signed JWT with KMS (short-lived local tokens), 3) scheduled vendor throttling drills. Need owners/timelines.

lizzie: I'll take vendor contract/SLA work. Action: legal + vendor mgmt call this week to negotiate dedicated auth endpoint and 99.95% issuance SLA. Deliverable: proposed SLA language and escalation contacts by 2026-04-08.

sasha: For KMS-based fallback: proposal is to pre-sign tokens for a limited scope and let services accept them if vendor is degraded. That requires sync with security and model-registry. I'll draft the architecture doc. ETA: draft by 2026-04-05.

raj: Quick mitigation script (for ops): 
```
# fallback: use cached token when vendor errors
if resp.status in [500, 429]:
  use_cached_token()
else:
  validate_and_cache(resp.token)
```
Will include tests in PR.

maria: Also recommending a synthetic check that hits vendor token endpoint at 1/min with randomized headers to catch early rate anomalies. Add to synthetic-monitoring dashboard by 3/29.

deploy-bot: Staging deploy scheduled: raj/token-cache-patch -> 2026-03-28 03:00 UTC. CI status: pending.

ammar: Owners summary (please confirm):
- Short-term token cache + jitter: raj (PR -> 3/27, staging 3/28)
- Alerting + playbook + synth-check: maria (3/29)
- Vendor SLA + escalation contacts: lizzie (4/08)
- KMS-signed token fallback architecture: sasha (4/05)
- Runbook drill + ops dry-run: ops rotation (owner TBD) -> schedule after staging deploy (target week of 4/12)

lizzie: Confirmed for SLA work. I'll set up vendor meeting and add to calendar.

sasha: Confirmed on architecture draft. I'll include a compatibility matrix for model-registry and hosted-inference consumers.

raj: Confirmed on PR and tests. I'll link the PR here when opened.

maria: Confirmed on alerts + dashboards.

ammar: One more recurring-incident item: add quarterly dependency resilience review for top-10 vendors (auth, model-registry, cloud infra). Assign to platform reliability. I'll add to the ops roadmap.

maria: Suggest we add a metric card in Console named "Vendor Auth Health" with green/yellow/red and runbook link — I'll prototype.

ammar: OK — action items recorded in the postmortem doc under "Follow-ups". Let's reconvene in 1 week for status: 2026-03-30 16:00 PT. If any blockers, ping in this thread. :thumbsup:
